title: Lockstep network-policy Terraform module: security groups, NACLs, private DNS, and egress gateway
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (lockstep-network-policy) to standardize VPC security controls for Private deployments. The module will manage service-tier security groups, subnet-level NACLs with default-deny templates, private DNS forwarding/resolver records, and a centralized egress gateway pattern (domain-aware allowlist). It must include a clear upgrade path and CI health checks so Dedicated/Private customers can adopt safely.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes composable inputs for control-plane, worker, and admin security group rules
Subnet NACLs default to deny with an audited allowlist and automatic idempotent reconciliation
Private DNS supports forwarding to customer resolvers and consents for split-horizon records
Egress gateway implements FQDN-based allowlist with TLS passthrough for approved destinations and metrics exported to CloudWatch/Prometheus
Module is compatible with Terraform 1.5+ and AWS provider 4.x/5.x and has semantic versioning (v1.0.0+)
Automated Terratest integration in CI validates basic connectivity, egress rules, and private DNS resolution in ephemeral test VPCs
Upgrade guide documents breaking changes and provides a canary rollout procedure for live VPCs
implementation_notes: Security groups: provide named rule sets (control-plane, compute, admin) and allow customers to pass additional security-group blocks for extensions
NACLs: use stateful-like patterns for ephemeral workloads; keep short, human-readable rule descriptions for audit tooling
Egress gateway: implement as an optional autoscaled appliance (ALB -> egress service) plus network-path controls; prefer domain-based rules (FQDN) over IP lists where possible
Private DNS: module should create hosted-private-zone records and conditional forwarders; do not overwrite existing customer records by default
Upgrade strategy: avoid default changes to deny/allow behavior on minor releases; breaking-behavior gated behind major version bump and a migration script in tools/migrations
Providers: vendor lock-in minimized by using provider-agnostic Terraform constructs where possible and isolating AWS-specific code behind local modules

risks: Changing default deny/allow semantics during upgrades could break customer workloads if applied automatically
FQDN-based egress relies on DNS resolution semantics; split-horizon setups introduce edge cases
Egress gateway appliance adds single point of failure unless customers enable multi-AZ auto-scaling
Testing across multiple customer topologies (on-prem connected VPCs, VPNs) increases QA surface area

Upgrade test: run module upgrade on a cloned staging VPC and validate no traffic regression
